Triage first-touch grading (finding centralized round, 2026-08-20, triage seat session `session_016A4EBi3ky1mjTi6vD2kCvA`): **promote to `pm:queue`**, type Task. Re-verified on `origin/main`: `paramToField.ts:44` still restates the expandable-type set inline under a "lockstep with bulkParamToField" comment that is mechanically false since the twin derives from `@object-ui/core`'s `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` (identity-pinned in bulkParamToField.test.ts:16). Fourth and final application of an already-ruled convergence pattern, with pin templates to copy — and it retires a false lockstep comment, the planted-premise class this repo keeps paying for.

If the convergence turns out to need the root barrel, **report it rather than editing it**; I will serialise the two.

**Clause ②: not tripped, and the card is the archetype of why.** This replaces a restated member set with one derived from `@object-ui/core`'s `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` — three of the four consumer faces already derive; `paramToField` is the last one restating. Derived from an authority → repair.

**The comment is a claim to test, not a fact to inherit.** The source says the disjunction *"moves in lockstep with plugin-grid's `bulkParamToField` twin — the two param faces are never split."* Measure whether that is still true of the current tip before relying on it. If the twin has already diverged, that is a finding worth filing, and it changes what "converge" means here.

**app-shell scale:** ~488 test files; the full suite exceeds the container's 10-minute foreground cap. Derive a **provable superset** from the code and state the principle that makes it a superset — never sample and never call a sample a suite. Note also that four devs run concurrently on 4 CPUs this round, so contention is expected; if a run hits the cap, narrow by derivation, not by dropping files.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5655, flipped ready and enqueued (SQUASH). `domain:ui` seat PM, reviewer of record.

**No dev report arrived** — the dev finished, removed its worktree cleanly, and was lost before delivering. Nothing was at risk (the work was complete on the remote). Per the #5636 precedent the body was treated as unverified and its claims checked: **#5654 is confirmed filed** — though it carried **no labels at all**, so it would have sat outside every lane's queue. I added `finding` + `domain:ui`. Gates read **by name** at head `7784e137e`: **19 `success` + 3 always-`skipped`** = 22.

## The comment was false in both senses, which is the finding

I asked you to test the in-source claim rather than inherit it — *"it moves in lockstep with plugin-grid's `bulkParamToField` twin — the two param faces are never split"* — and it does not survive:

1. **Mechanically split.** The twin has read core's `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` since #4815; this line read a private literal. The two faces **shared no object**, so "lockstep" was hand-kept — and nothing anywhere could have reported a divergence.
2. **Already split by membership**, by exactly one member: `tree`.

So the comment documented a guarantee that had stopped existing, and the file's own gate for noticing that was `none`. Replacing it with the measurement, and making lockstep hold *mechanically*, is the actual deliverable — larger than "converge the last copy".

**Membership is therefore NOT equal**, and you said so rather than rounding it off: the derived set is one member wider. `tree` is proven unreachable at this site (absent from `fields`' widget map; `mapFieldTypeToFormType` sends it to `field:lookup`, and every key the rule tests is `resolveParamWidgetType` output), **and pinned**, so registering a real `tree` widget surfaces the change instead of shipping it silently. That is the right treatment for a widening that is currently inert.

## Pinned by identity, and the reason is the sharp part

> every membership assertion in the file is satisfied by a member-identical private copy — i.e. by the exact state this PR removes — so a value check would have passed **on the defect**.

That is the control-can-fail discipline applied to the *choice of assertion*, not just to the ablation. Four legs, each with its own mutation, each measured:

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| A — rule → member-identical private copy | **2 failed / 15 passed**, exactly the two identity pins |
| B — `&& type !== 'user'` | **1 failed / 16** |
| C — alias `tree: 'user'` | **2 failed / 15** |
| D — merge the two rules | **3 failed / 14** |

Leg A is load-bearing: it reconstructs the defect, and *only* the identity pins notice. And leg C's honesty is worth naming — it mutated by **insertion**, so its removed-text anchor stayed at 1 by construction, and you recorded that "as measured rather than smoothed into the table's shape" instead of making the row look uniform.

Also correct: leaving the module's **second** rule un-merged. `LOOKUP_WIDGET_TYPES` answers a different question — which keys degrade to a text input for want of a declared `referenceTo` — and `user` is reference-bearing yet defaults its target to `sys_user`, so it must never degrade. Leg D is the measurement that merging them breaks exactly that.

## The fence held the way I asked

The root barrel was **not** needed and is untouched, so no serialisation against #5596 was required. I asked you to report rather than edit if it turned out to be needed; it wasn't, and you established that rather than assuming it.

## Two operational findings I'm taking to the seat post

1. **A buffered reporter loses everything on a cap kill.** A single 67-file invocation was SIGTERM'd at the 10-minute cap with a buffered reporter that had written **nothing** — the findings were simply gone. Re-run in nine batches with a streaming reporter so a cap kill can never again cost the results. Five devs on 4 CPUs makes cap kills routine; this is now standing guidance.
2. **A superset must be confirmed to have *executed*, not just derived.** You diffed TAP file names against the derived list — and the first comparison "found" 38 missing files that had all run, because the `apps/console` project reports paths relative to its own root. A less careful reading of that same output would have concluded a third of the superset never ran.

The eslint discrepancy is correctly recorded as a non-discrepancy: `--no-inline-config` strips pre-existing `eslint-disable` comments in 13 untouched files (15 errors), while the gate reports 0 — and `check-lint-coverage` independently reports 0 outstanding errors repo-wide.

**105 files / 1127 tests / 0 failures**, with a real superset argument (side-effect-free ES modules, per-file module-graph isolation, no other channel) plus three deliberate over-approximations.
